items.name: theme
items.title: FIVIC Theme
items.description: The Flooring Innovations Victoria brand as tokens, worked out in OKLCH from the logo and fivic.net. Install this first, once per app, before anything else. Five ramps built on the same set of lightness steps, a disabled pair so no control has to fall back on an opacity, every named colour in light and dark, a 14px type scale, 4px radius and tighter spacing than shadcn ships. One thing to watch: --brand (#2997B0) and --primary (#177B91) are different colours on purpose. Brand is identity only and primary carries anything with words on it, because white on the logo teal fails WCAG AA. See AGENTS.md. Install the fonts item alongside this.

theme.font-mono: ui-monospace, "SF Mono", SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace

items.name: fonts
items.title: Self-hosted Brand Fonts
items.description: @font-face rules for Bai Jamjuree, which only goes 20px and up and never sets a number, and Inter variable, which does all the UI and data with tabular figures. Nothing is loaded off Google's servers, because a FIVIC app never calls out to anyone else while it's running. Comes with a script you run once at setup that pulls the woff2 files into public/fonts/. Both families are SIL Open Font License 1.1.

items.name: agents
items.title: Agent Conventions
items.description: Rules for any agent working on FIVIC OS, in code or in the Figma file. Install from this registry, theme first, don't mix up --brand and --primary, never write a colour value in a component, numbers are always tabular, Bai Jamjuree never sets a number, 32px controls instead of 36px, both modes in one commit, and nothing calls out to another server. It also says which type step goes where, that everything is sentence case, and carries the Figma file keys, the variable modes and the plugin API traps. Put this in every app and every repo.

items.name: logo
items.title: Brand Mark
items.description: The fivic mark as a React component. It draws from currentColor, so one component covers brand teal on light, white on dark, and muted when something's turned off. FivicMark for the raw shape, FivicLogo for the mark at --brand. The full lockup with the wordmark isn't in here, that needs fivic's vector artwork, which we haven't got yet.

items.name: button
items.title: Button
items.description: The FIVIC button. 32px by default instead of shadcn's 36px, because up and down space is the scarcest thing on these screens. The filled one uses --primary, and there's deliberately no brand variant, because white on the logo teal fails WCAG AA. Sizes are sm (28px, inline and in table rows), default (32px), and lg (36px, for the one main action on a page). The label is text-label at all three: size changes the control, not the type. A trailingIcon prop puts an icon after the label, for a button that opens something rather than doing something, which is the one thing you cannot compose from children.

items.name: select
items.title: FIVIC Select
items.description: A dropdown trigger built to match Input rather than Button, because a control holding a value you chose should look like the controls holding values you typed: 32px, --input border, --card fill, radius-md, text-label. Sizes are sm (28px) and default (32px), the same two the Button has, and there is no lg because a select is never the main action on a page. Two variants: default is the bordered trigger, and ghost drops the border, the fill and the type step so it can sit inside a table cell without drawing a box around one column. Restyled on the shadcn Select, not forked from it.

items.name: status-chip
items.title: Status Chip
items.description: The one place state gets named and coloured in FIVIC OS. Almost every list row carries a state, and without a single component the same state ends up named three ways and coloured four. Tones are success (settled), warning (needs a person to look at it), danger (rejected or failed), info (the system did it, nobody's confirmed it yet), and neutral. Measured at 4.5:1 or better in both modes.

items.name: input
items.title: Input
items.description: The FIVIC text field. The same box as the Select trigger on purpose: 32px, radius-md, --card fill, --input border and 10px of side padding, so a value you typed and a value you picked read as one family. The value is text-body-sm rather than text-label, because it is content the person wrote, and the placeholder is --muted-foreground. --input is a border colour, never a fill. In Figma the Input is the search field with a 14px leading icon and a Clear boolean. This is the bare input element and the app composes the search field out of it. Disabled is tokens, not opacity.

items.name: checkbox
items.title: Checkbox
items.description: The FIVIC checkbox, on Radix. 13px rather than shadcn's 16px, because it sits in 36px rows next to a 12px label, at radius-xs. Checked fills with --primary and carries the tick in --primary-foreground, unchecked is a bare --input border. 13px is too small to aim at, so always wrap it in a label or make the row the label, and the words become the hit area. Disabled drops the checked fill to --disabled, the same way a disabled Button drops its variant.

items.name: switch
items.title: Switch
items.description: The FIVIC switch, on Radix. Only for something that takes effect the moment it flips. If the setting waits for a Save button, use a Checkbox. 28x16 with a 12px knob. On is --primary with a --primary-foreground knob, off is --secondary with a --card knob, disabled is --disabled with a --disabled-foreground knob. The knob is what tells off from disabled, because --secondary and --disabled are the same neutral step, so don't restyle it.

items.name: avatar
items.title: Avatar
items.description: A person, as initials or a photo, on Radix. Sizes are default (26px) and sm (20px, inside something dense like a question card, a citation or an RFI row). --accent fill, --border stroke, initials in --accent-foreground. The initials are 11px at weight 600 with zero tracking, which is off the type scale on purpose, because caption's 2% tracking drags centred initials left. That size is written once, inside this component, and nowhere else.

items.name: segmented-control
items.title: Segmented control
items.description: Two or three segments splitting a panel's width evenly, on Radix Tabs so it gets tablist roles and arrow keys. It replaces the panel's title rather than sitting under one. 38px tall with a --border-subtle rule along the bottom. The selected segment is --foreground with a 2px --brand bar underneath, the rest are --muted-foreground. Labels are text-label and don't change weight when selected, since that shifted the width by a pixel. Counts go in the label through the count prop, on text-caption in --muted-foreground, never in a badge.

items.name: split-divider
items.title: Split divider
items.description: The bar between two resizable panes, on react-resizable-panels v4, which already does double click to reset, keyboard resizing and a remembered layout. SplitGroup takes splits="top and bottom" or "left and right", named for what gets split rather than which way the bar runs, and maps it to the library's orientation. A 5px --border-subtle bar with a 34x14 handle at radius-sm (--card fill, --border stroke, 12px grip) and 11px of grab area. The app still owes minSize on both panels, a snap to a floor within 24px, a visible collapse control and the split remembered per person starting at 55%. Panel sizes in v4 are pixels as numbers and percentages as strings.
